name: is-a-plan
points: The output proposes one concrete change and names the files it edits.
The output says where a reopened session's transcript comes from after the change.

name: no-marks
points: The plan does not tell untyped text apart by its wording: it puts no prefix, tag, or sentinel in a message's text, and the reader matches no pattern in the text.
The plan adds no key, flag, or label to a message to say whether it is shown.
No rule in the plan decides whether a message is shown from where or when it was added, such as during a handoff.

name: model-input-unchanged
points: The plan changes no file under lib/runtime/.
The plan adds no parameter or option to a public stdlib function such as userMessage or llm.
The model is sent the same messages with the same text as before the change: nothing on the conversation thread is split, moved, added, or removed.

name: own-record
points: The transcript is a record written as each turn happens, by code that receives the text the user typed. It is not rebuilt from the conversation thread.
The record is saved with the run's checkpoint, so a cancelled turn's entry goes away with the turn and a forked session gets its own copy.
The plan makes sure the recorded text is exactly what the user typed: it finds the cancel note the driver joins onto the message and keeps that note out of the record.
The code that reads the record out of a saved session does not depend on a source file's path or on a variable name in another file.

name: covers-the-cases
points: The plan names slash commands as a case, and after the change a reopened session shows the /command the user typed, not its expanded prompt.
The plan names the compaction summary as a case, and after the change a reopened session does not show the summary as something the user said.
The plan names a subagent's messages as a case, and after the change a reopened session shows the turn's final reply, not the subagent's messages as replies.
The plan says what a session saved before the change shows when it is reopened, and that session still shows its earlier turns.
The plan says what happens to the callers of the transcript reader: either they need no change, or it names each caller it updates.
